rationales.eli10: The receptor is the sensor that first notices something changed.

questions.stem: Touching a hot surface causes rapid withdrawal before conscious awareness. Why?

options.text: The spinal cord integrates the reflex

rationales.whyCorrect: A spinal circuit activates flexors quickly while sensory information also ascends to the brain.
rationales.eli10: The spinal cord orders a quick pull-away while the news travels to your brain.

questions.stem: What sympathetic effect helps deliver more oxygen during exercise?

rationales.whyCorrect: Sympathetic stimulation widens airways and supports increased ventilation.
rationales.eli10: Air tubes open wider so more air can move.

questions.stem: Which parasympathetic effect commonly occurs after a meal?

rationales.whyCorrect: Parasympathetic signals enhance gastrointestinal secretion and motility.
rationales.eli10: The body turns up its food-processing machinery after eating.

questions.stem: A mixed spinal nerve is cut. Which functions may be lost?

rationales.whyCorrect: Spinal nerves contain both afferent and efferent axons.
rationales.eli10: A mixed nerve has wires traveling both toward and away from the spinal cord.

questions.stem: Damage to a dorsal root most directly causes what deficit?

options.text: Reduced sensory input at that spinal level

rationales.whyCorrect: Dorsal roots carry afferent fibers into the spinal cord.
rationales.eli10: The incoming doorway for sensory messages is damaged.

questions.stem: Damage to a ventral root affects what most directly?

options.text: Motor output from that spinal level

rationales.whyCorrect: Ventral roots carry efferent axons away from the spinal cord.
rationales.eli10: The outgoing doorway for movement commands is damaged.

questions.stem: Which response is expected during sympathetic activation?

rationales.whyCorrect: Sympathetic output raises cardiac rate and contractility to support activity.
rationales.eli10: The heart pumps faster to send more blood during an emergency.

questions.stem: All autonomic preganglionic neurons release which neurotransmitter?

rationales.whyCorrect: Both sympathetic and parasympathetic preganglionic fibers are cholinergic.
rationales.eli10: The first neuron in either automatic pathway uses the same chemical message.

questions.stem: Most sympathetic postganglionic neurons release what?

rationales.whyCorrect: Norepinephrine is the usual sympathetic transmitter at target organs, with exceptions such as sweat glands.
rationales.eli10: Most second sympathetic wires use norepinephrine to alert organs.

questions.stem: Why does the pupil dilate during sympathetic activation?

options.text: To admit more light for visual alertness

rationales.whyCorrect: Radial iris muscle contraction enlarges the pupil during fight-or-flight responses.
rationales.eli10: The eye's opening gets wider to gather more visual information.

questions.stem: The knee-jerk response uses one sensory neuron synapsing directly on one motor neuron. What type is it?

rationales.whyCorrect: The stretch reflex's central excitatory pathway contains a single synapse.
rationales.eli10: The sensor passes its message straight to the movement neuron.

questions.stem: Why can a crushed peripheral nerve sometimes recover better than a severed CNS tract?

options.text: Schwann-cell pathways can guide regrowing axons

rationales.whyCorrect: If the soma and connective pathway survive, Schwann cells support peripheral regeneration.
rationales.eli10: Surviving guide tunnels can help a damaged outside nerve wire grow toward its target.

questions.stem: A sensory receptor adapts rapidly to constant pressure. What does the person mainly notice?

options.text: The beginning and end of the pressure

rationales.whyCorrect: Rapidly adapting receptors emphasize changes rather than sustained stimuli.
rationales.eli10: You notice putting on a watch, then soon stop noticing it until it moves.

questions.stem: Which cranial nerve carries major parasympathetic output to thoracic and abdominal organs?

rationales.whyCorrect: The vagus nerve supplies parasympathetic fibers to the heart, lungs, and much of the digestive tract.
rationales.eli10: The vagus is a long calm-down nerve reaching many chest and belly organs.

questions.stem: Why is autonomic control described as a two-neuron chain?

options.text: Two sensory neurons enter each receptor
Two motor neurons innervate skeletal muscle
One neuron stays entirely in a gland
Preganglionic and postganglionic neurons connect CNS to effector

rationales.whyCorrect: The neurons synapse in an autonomic ganglion before reaching the visceral target.
rationales.eli10: One wire reaches a relay station, and a second wire reaches the organ.

questions.stem: Why can sympathetic activation affect many organs at once?

options.text: Preganglionic fibers diverge widely and adrenal hormones circulate
Every organ shares one motor neuron
Sympathetic signals travel only through blood

rationales.whyCorrect: Neural divergence and adrenal catecholamines create a coordinated whole-body response.
rationales.eli10: One alarm branches to many places, and the blood carries extra alarm chemicals.

questions.stem: A spinal reflex remains present after loss of communication with the brain. What does this demonstrate?

options.text: The spinal cord contains a complete local integration circuit
Sensory receptors lie in the brain

rationales.whyCorrect: Receptor, afferent neuron, spinal integration, efferent neuron, and effector can produce the response locally.
rationales.eli10: The spinal cord can run a quick safety loop without waiting for the brain.

questions.stem: A drug blocks nicotinic receptors in autonomic ganglia. Which pathways are affected?

rationales.whyCorrect: Preganglionic neurons in both divisions release acetylcholine onto ganglionic nicotinic receptors.
rationales.eli10: Both automatic systems use the same kind of receiver at their relay stations.

questions.stem: Why does parasympathetic activity usually produce more localized effects than sympathetic activity?

options.text: Its pathways diverge less and ganglia lie near targets

rationales.whyCorrect: Limited branching permits more discrete control of individual organs.
rationales.eli10: Its calm messages go to selected rooms instead of sounding a building-wide alarm.

questions.stem: A peripheral axon is cut, but its cell body survives and the endoneurial tube remains aligned. What best predicts recovery?

options.text: Axonal sprouts may grow through the tube toward the target
The cell body immediately becomes a glial cell
The distal segment reconnects without degeneration
The CNS replaces the nerve with bone

rationales.whyCorrect: An intact connective path and Schwann-cell support improve peripheral regeneration.
rationales.eli10: A new wire tip can follow the old tunnel back to its destination.

questions.stem: During standing, a drop in blood pressure triggers sympathetic activity and reduced parasympathetic activity. Why are both changes useful?

options.text: Together they increase cardiac output and vascular tone
Together they increase intestinal blood flow only

rationales.whyCorrect: Reciprocal autonomic adjustments raise heart rate and constrict vessels to restore pressure.
